newsitem.title: USA: Midwest Cash Grain PM -Most corn, soy basis flat.
newsitem.headline: Midwest Cash Grain PM -Most corn, soy basis flat.

text.p: Most corn and soybean basis bids were steady or registered little change Thursday as many farmers continued to focus on fieldwork, dealers said.
"If they're not out in the fields, then they are thinking about planting," an Ohio dealer said.
Some dealers reported a moderate pickup in wheat sales after CBOT futures rallied their 20-cent limit.
"We saw an increase in business later on in the afternoon, but you have to remember that farmers have seen these prices before," a merchandiser said.
One soybean processor said it would continue to be hard to buy beans because most farmers are waiting for higher prices.
"This is a flat price market right now," the dealer said. "All our hedging has been done, and the farmer is waiting for $9.00 (per bushel) beans."
High water on the Mississippi River continued to cause problems for some merchandisers, they said.
The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers has closed most locks from St. Anthony Falls, Minn., south to the lock at New Boston Ill., so there is little traffic on the river, dealers said.
Basis values are quoted against CBOT futures, cash $/bu.
Note: UNQ=Unquoted. K=CBOT May, N=CBOT July
